This episode differs because co-lending arrangements between NBFCs and banks represent a deeply integrated, symbiotic partnership rather than a simple corporate favor or management service. However, just like those past tax-net expansions, the underlying fiscal logic—targeting invisible financial intermediation margins that escape direct taxation—remains identical. Unlike online gaming, where the service recipient is an individual consumer with no recourse, taxing NBFC services to banks creates an immediate circular feedback loop into the cost of capital for priority sectors, creating profound policy friction that stalled past multi-layered financial service taxation proposals like the reverse charge mechanism on certain supplies.
